question.problem: Given that $p(x,y)=2x+{y}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂p}{∂\theta },$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $p(x,y)$ with two independent variables $r$ and $\theta ,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂p}{∂\theta } & =\frac{∂p}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂\theta }+\frac{∂p}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂\theta } \\  & =-\frac{∂p}{∂x}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{∂p}{∂y}r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $n$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂p}{∂x}=2,\,\frac{∂p}{∂y}=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r$ and $\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂p}{∂x} & =2, \\ \frac{∂p}{∂y} & =2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂p}{∂\theta } & =-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +(2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & ={r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
